fizzle.quote: TFP effects within the next 10 years should be no more than 0.66% in total – or approximately a 0.064% increase in TFP growth annually.

number.note: Opened the MIT PDF of Economic Policy 2024. Headline claim is 0.66% TFP over 10 years; Acemoglu's own annualisation is 0.064pp/year. The tighter easy/hard split ('less than 0.53%' over 10 years) is a further downward adjustment of the same estimate, not a second claim. We take his stated annualisation of the headline number.

fab.who: Joseph Briggs and Devesh Kodnani, Goldman Sachs Research
fab.quote: lift productivity growth by 1.5 percentage points over a 10-year period

number.note: Public GS summary of Briggs/Kodnani, 26 March 2023, 'The Potentially Large Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Economic Growth'. The note itself says 'raise annual US labor productivity growth by just under 1½pp over a 10-year period following widespread adoption' and 'around 1.5pp/year'.

fab.quote: Demand growth is actually the way to drive down the price.

number.note: Claim has no figure; anchor set to the weakest form of it (premium does not widen) and flagged as ours, not his.

doom.who: Manuel Abecasis and Hongcen Wei, Goldman Sachs Research
doom.quote: we expect consumer electricity inflation to remain around 6% in 2026-2027

number.note: Primary GS note 'The Macroeconomic Spillovers From AI Electricity Demand', 11 Feb 2026. They attribute the path to data-center demand (about 40% of power-demand growth) plus utility capex passed into rates. Institutional forecast, not a named decelerationist — but it is a named, dated, opposite bet to Wright on the direction of prices.
